openQuestions.title: Force a style flush after the timed class change, or explain why not
openQuestions.detail: breakpoint-animation (the listener at ~line 129) toggles the 'lit' class without a getComputedStyle() flush afterwards, so the transition is only created at the next style recalc, which Chrome runs after animation frame callbacks. A "1 frame late" reading can therefore come from style-resolution timing, not from transitionrun dispatch deferral — the frames-to-run run reported the plain setTimeout task as "1 iteration late" too, which is consistent with that artefact. Either flush style immediately after the timed change (as the reset path already does) or document why the unflushed case is the right measurement, then re-verify on a Chrome build known to carry the fix.

openQuestions.title: Verify the same-iteration success path on a Chrome build that ships the change
openQuestions.detail: Chromium 153.0.8010.12 headless still shows every crossing one iteration late; neither the page nor this pass identified a runtime flag (none found under that name in runtime_enabled_features.json5). Identify the base::Feature/flag or the build that carries the change, record it on the page, and capture a 0-frame run.
